wage_context: High female spinning wages relative to the jenny's capital cost made labor savings valuable.
adoption_result: The modeled jenny investment earned a high return
calculation_scope: Allen's most-likely case: a 24-spindle jenny tripled productivity; the spinner worked about 40% of full time; machine life was ten years.
limits: A modeled private return for one textile technology—not a national invention rate or proof that prices alone caused industrialization.

wage_context: Lower spinning wages reduced the value of labor saved relative to the machine's cost.
adoption_result: The same modeled investment barely paid
calculation_scope: Allen applies comparable productivity and utilization assumptions using French wage and capital-price evidence.
limits: The estimate is sensitive to wage, price, utilization, maintenance, and productivity assumptions.

wage_context: Much lower estimated spinning wages made labor substitution a loss under the central assumptions.
calculation_scope: Allen estimates Indian female spinning earnings and applies the same central productivity and utilization case.
limits: The Indian wage estimate is less direct; Allen also reports alternative scenarios, so this central result is not a universal return.
